name: Gold facial

card.summary: A spa facial in which gold leaf, gold-infused masks or serums are applied to the face, offered with the aim of a brighter, smoother-looking, luxurious skin finish.
card.note: Spa claims about gold's skin effects are largely untested in published human studies.

quick.overview:
A gold facial is a salon or spa treatment in which gold, often described as 24-karat, is applied to the skin as leaf, flakes, powder-infused masks or serums, usually inside an otherwise standard facial routine. Spas offer it for a radiant, even-looking complexion and a pampering experience.

Facials in general are skincare treatments that can include steam, exfoliation, extraction, masks, peels and massage [1]. Gold is long associated with luxury in food and decoration [2]. Published clinical trials of gold facials specifically were not found.
quick.how: It is performed by an aesthetician as part of a facial session: skin is cleansed and prepared, a gold-containing mask or leaf is applied, and massage and moisturizer typically follow. Many people treat it as an occasional event rather than a routine.
quick.risks: Facials can cause temporary redness or breakouts in some people, and anyone with a metal allergy or sensitive skin may ask the provider about ingredients first. Cosmetic products vary by manufacturer.

lead: A gold facial is a spa treatment that adds gold, commonly sold as 24k gold leaf or a gold-infused mask, to a facial. Providers market it for a luminous, smoother-looking complexion and as a luxury experience.

Facials are a family of skincare treatments given at salons and spas that may include steam, exfoliation, extractions, masks, peels and massage; they support general skin appearance and can address particular concerns [1]. The gold element is an add-on within that format.

Gold leaf has a long history as a decorative luxury material, used on food, drinks and sculpture; as a food additive it is designated E175 [2]. No published human trials of gold facials were identified.

chain: Gold-containing mask or leaf applied within a facial
Massage, hydration and mask steps leave skin looking temporarily bright and smooth
Fresher-looking complexion for a few days
angle.text: Providers present gold as adding radiance and a premium finish. Any immediate glow likely reflects the cleansing, massage and moisturizing steps of the facial itself, which are well-established components of facial treatments.

paras: Gold facials are sold under names such as 24k gold facial and gold mask. They sit within the broader facial category, which Wikipedia defines as skincare treatments for the face usually given in beauty salons and spas [1]. Gold itself is used in leaf form for decoration of food and objects, a practice traced back thousands of years, and is approved as a food additive with the code E175 [2].
Spas describe benefits such as brightening, firming and antioxidant effects. These are marketing claims made by providers; the wiki does not find published clinical studies testing them.
